editorial.headline: Second-Hand Building Materials: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This retail activity is nationally open to PMA ownership of up to 100%, yet Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for it today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 47745 covers the retail trade of used construction materials and used sanitary ware. Its practical territory is the resale of items such as second-hand sinks, toilets and water tanks: goods that have already had one life in a building and are being offered again through retail trade. The scope also expressly places direct sales alongside that activity. It is a focused commercial category, concerned with the retail circulation of used building and sanitation fixtures rather than a broad claim over the construction economy.

Nationally, the classification is marked **TERBUKA** for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The national reference recorded for it is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain terms, the national setting does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. That is the national position founders should begin with—but it is not the final answer for a business intending to register in Bali.

The code is open across the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That breadth matters because the activity may be structured at any of those stated business scales; the record does not reserve this resale trade for one particular size of operator. A founder should therefore define the business by what it actually sells—used construction materials and sanitary goods—and by the retail activity described here, rather than assuming that the national PMA setting alone settles the location question.

In Bali, the answer is decisive: a PMA business cannot register this activity there today. Bali classifies it as **Blocked (risk class)**. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent block on all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The recorded reason ties that result to the Bali moratorium of May 2026, with the cited source being Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The national 100% ceiling remains the national ceiling; in Bali, however, the moratorium prevents PMA registration for this code.
editorial.pullQuote: The national 100% ceiling remains intact, but Bali’s moratorium prevents PMA registration for this activity today.
